name: Capabilities Encoding Benchmark for Remote Sensing
description: Foundation models constitute a significant advancement in computer vision: after a single, albeit costly, training phase, they can address a wide array of tasks. In the field of Earth observation, over 75 remote sensing vision foundation models have been developed in the past four years. However, none has consistently outperformed the others across all available downstream tasks. To facilitate their comparison, we propose a cost-effective method for predicting a model's performance on multiple downstream tasks without the need for fine-tuning on each one. This method is based on what we call "capabilities encoding." The utility of this novel approach is twofold: we demonstrate its potential to simplify the selection of a foundation model for a given new task, and we employ it to offer a fresh perspective on the existing literature, suggesting avenues for future research. Codes are available at https://github.com/pierreadorni/capabilities-encoding.
evaluation_method: Spearman/Pearson correlation and RMSE between predicted and actual downstream performance
reputation: A recent research contribution proposing a cost‑effective meta-evaluation method for remote sensing foundation models; adoption is still emerging.
notes: Utility depends on the diversity and representativeness of chosen downstream tasks; does not substitute for task-specific fine-tuning and may not generalize across very different task families or data distributions.
